Serving as Japan's prime minister from 2010 to 2011, this politician was the first in years to hold the post for more than twelve months, and later published a memoir titled 'Fifty Years of Citizen Politics' — who is he?
Naoto Kan: Prime Minister of Japan from 2010 to 2011. On 26 August 2011, Kan announced his resignation.

Fought from 1688 to 1697, this European conflict pitted Louis XIV's France against a Grand Alliance, with spillover fighting in Ireland and a North American front called King William's War — what was it?
Nine Years' War: War between France and a European coalition (1688–1697)

Announced by President Bush after the September 11 attacks, this was the official U.S. name for the first phase (2001-2014) of the Afghanistan war against al-Qaeda and the Taliban — what was it called?
Operation Enduring Freedom: Official name for the US's war on terror.
This Wisconsin Republican served as the 54th Speaker of the House from 2015 to 2019 and was Mitt Romney's running mate in the 2012 presidential election — who is he?
India's longest-serving Minister of Commerce and Industry, this politician also won the 2018 Carnot Prize for his work in energy policy — who is he?

Fought almost entirely at sea from 1798 to 1800 after France began seizing American ships, this undeclared conflict pitted the young United States against the French First Republic — what was it called?
Quasi-War: Undeclared naval war between the United States and France, 1798–1800.

During the French Revolution, this period saw waves of public executions ordered by the Committee of Public Safety, with some historians dating its start to the Law of Suspects in September 1793 — what is this era known as?
Reign of Terror: 1793–1794 period of political violence during the French Revolution.
Elected in 1987 as the first South Korean president chosen by direct popular vote, this former army general had earlier helped his military academy friend seize power in a 1979 coup. Who is he?
Roh Tae-woo: President of South Korea from 1988 to 1993.
Born Rozbih Khwushbudhan and trained as a Zoroastrian magus, this companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad converted to Islam after meeting him in Medina — who was he?

Salman the Persian: Companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. Muhammad specifically said "Salman is part of my Ahl al-Bayt." In meetings with the other companions, he was often referred to by the kunya Abu ʿAbdullah.

For 17 years Carthage and Rome struggled for Mediterranean supremacy across Italy, Iberia, and North Africa, with Hannibal repeatedly crushing Roman legions before Carthage's eventual defeat — which of their three wars was this?
Second Punic War: War between Rome and Carthage (218–201 BC)
Founded in 1966 by Bal Thackeray as a Marathi nationalist, Hindutva-based movement, this Indian political party split into two rival factions in 2022 — what is it called?
Shiv Sena: Political party in Maharashtra, India.

Lasting from December 1979 to February 1989, this conflict saw mujahideen fighters — backed by Pakistan, the U.S. via Operation Cyclone, and others — battle a Communist superpower and its allied government. What war is it?
Soviet–Afghan War: 1979–1989 armed conflict in South Asia.
A London School of Economics graduate from a wealthy family, he led Togo from its 1958 election to independence as prime minister and then president, until his 1963 assassination — who was he?

Sylvanus Olympio: President of Togo from 1960 to 1963. After World War II, Olympio became prominent in efforts for independence of Togo and his party won the 1958 election, making him the prime minister of the country.
Founded by Aleister Crowley in the early 1900s, this occult philosophy centers on discovering one's 'True Will' and the maxim 'Do what thou wilt shall be the whole of the Law' — what is it?
Thelema: New religious movement founded by Aleister Crowley.

Elected by Ostrogothic nobles in 541 after his two predecessors were killed for trying to surrender to the Romans, this penultimate Gothic king reversed the tide of the Gothic War and recovered nearly all of Italy by 543 — who was he?
Totila: King of the Ostrogoths from 541 to 552.
The only woman ever to serve as chief minister of Rajasthan, this Indian politician also held two Cabinet posts under Atal Bihari Vajpayee — who is she?

Vasundhara Raje: 11th Chief Minister of Rajasthan. Vasundhara Raje Scindia (born 8 March 1953) is an Indian politician, who has held the position of the chief minister of Rajasthan from 2003 to 2008 and 2013 to 2018.
Deeply in debt to Adolf Hitler for loans he'd borrowed, this aristocratic field marshal commanded Germany's army during the Battle of France and the invasions of Yugoslavia and Greece - who was he?
Walther von Brauchitsch: German Commander-in-Chief during World War II (1881–1948)
The first Canadian prime minister to hold a PhD, this Liberal racked up 21 years and 154 days in office across three non-consecutive terms — the longest tenure in the country's history; who is he?
William Lyon Mackenzie King: Canadian prime minister (1874–1950)
Claiming to be Catherine the Great's dead husband Tsar Peter III, this Cossack leader proclaimed an end to serfdom in 1773 and led a massive peasant uprising across the Volga-Ural region. Who was he?
Yemelyan Pugachev: Russian Cossack rebel leader (1742–1775)
Nicknamed 'The Acquitator' for his string of courtroom wins as a criminal defense lawyer, he served as France's Minister of Justice from 2020 to 2024 — who is he?
Éric Dupond-Moretti: French-Italian politician and lawyer (born 1961)
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Frank Oppenheimer is a physicist. The younger brother of renowned physicist J.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Émilie du Châtelet is a mathematician. It circulated widely, generated heated debates, and was translated into German and Italian in 1743.
What is the atomic number of Hassium?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
What is the atomic number of Krypton?
Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.
In what year was Alfred Nobel born?
Alfred Nobel: Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
In what year was Kitty Oppenheimer born?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was John Maynard Keynes born?
John Maynard Keynes: Keynes was educated at King's College at the University of Cambridge, where he graduated in 1904 with a B.A. in mathematics.
In what year did Thales of Miletus die?
Thales of Miletus: Thales of Miletus ( THAY-leez; Ancient Greek: Θαλῆς; c. 626/623 – c. 548/545 BC) was an Ancient Greek pre-Socratic philosopher from Miletus in Ionia, Asia Minor.
In what year did Ernest Rutherford die?
Ernest Rutherford: Together with Thomas Royds, Rutherford is credited with proving that alpha radiation is composed of helium nuclei.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 from?

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Soviet Union. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Pyxis?
Pyxis: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pyxis is a small and faint constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Neodymium?
Neodymium: Carl Auer von Welsbach. Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Who is credited with discovering TON 618?
Who is credited with discovering Thallium?
Thallium: Claude-Auguste Lamy. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.

Produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, this mineralocorticoid is the body's key sodium-saver, quietly governing blood pressure and potassium balance in the kidney — which hormone is it?
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.

Usually a symptom of coronary artery disease caused by atherosclerosis narrowing the arteries, this chest pain or pressure gets its name from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest' — name this condition?
Angina is chest pain or pressure, usually caused by insufficient blood flow to the heart muscle (myocardium).
Sharing chemistry with phosphorus and antimony, this group-15 metalloid carries the symbol As and a notorious reputation for toxicity — what is it?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
The second-largest living rodents after capybaras, these large semiaquatic mammals of the Northern Hemisphere have webbed back feet, hand-like front paws, and flat, scaly tails — name the animal?
Beaver (genus Castor) are large semiaquatic rodents of the Northern Hemisphere.
Around 2,500 species of this insect family defend themselves by secreting a skin-irritating toxin called cantharidin, often flaunting bold warning colors — which family?
Blister beetle are beetles of the family Meloidae, so called for their defensive secretion of a blistering agent, cantharidin.

This British dog breed of mastiff type has a stocky build, a large head, thick facial skin folds, and a protruding lower jaw, and is now illegal to breed in the Netherlands over health concerns — name the breed?
Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
Seen as the frontman of Mexican neoliberalism, this economist-president championed and signed NAFTA after an election clouded by fraud accusations — who is he?
Carlos Salinas de Gortari (Spanish; born 3 April 1948) is a Mexican economist and former politician who served as the 60th president of Mexico from 1988 to 1994.
Patented in 1948 and used to treat hay fever and other allergic conditions, this first-generation antihistamine works within two hours by blocking the H1 histamine receptor — name the drug?
Chlorphenamine (CP, CPM), also known as chlorpheniramine, is an antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis (hay fever).

Ranging across most of Europe and into the Palearctic as far as northwestern China, this medium-sized bird of prey sees its northernmost populations migrate as far as South Africa each winter — which raptor?
Common buzzard (Buteo buteo) is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range.
Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
Birds are the only surviving lineage of these warmblooded Mesozoic reptiles, having evolved from theropods in the Late Jurassic — what is the broader group called?
Dinosaur are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.

This is the industrial process of converting other forms of energy into electric power, typically at power plants using electromechanical devices, before it is transmitted and distributed to end users. What is this process called?
Electricity generation is the process of generating electric power from sources of primary energy.

This simple hydrocarbon gas, the simplest member of a class called alkenes, is the most-produced organic compound on Earth by tonnage, and is the primary building block of a common plastic — what is it?
Ethylene (IUPAC name: ethene) is a hydrocarbon which has the formula C2H4 or H2C=CH2.
Using a skin membrane called a patagium plus a long tail for steering, these gliding rodents can sail from tree to tree without true flight — what are they called?
Flying squirrel (scientifically known as Pteromyini or Petauristini) are a tribe of 50 species of squirrels in the family Sciuridae.
Arriving late to a lecture, this mathematician copied down two famous unsolved problems thinking they were homework — and solved them; he's better known for the simplex algorithm, but who was he?

George Dantzig (November 8, 1914 - May 13, 2005) was an American mathematical scientist who made contributions to industrial engineering, operations research, computer science, economics and statistics.
Endemic to Africa and among the oldest of the gallinaceous birds, this family branched off before New World quail evolutionarily — name the birds?
Guinea fowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
Planted for land reclamation thanks to its nitrogen-fixing, erosion-resisting root system, this deciduous shrub genus's berries also show up in human and animal food products — what genus is it?
Hippophae is a genus of flowering plants in the family Elaeagnaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
A Scottish surgeon who corrected clubfoot and squints, he's also dubbed by some the 'Father of Modern Hypnotism' — pioneering both hypnotic and chemical anaesthesia. Who was this gentleman scientist?
James Braid (surgeon) (19 June 1795 - 25 March 1860) was a Scottish surgeon, natural philosopher, and "gentleman scientist".

An evergreen conifer in the cypress family, this small tree or shrub boasts the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere — which species?
Juniperus communis is a species of small tree or shrub in the cypress family Cupressaceae.
Native to the Mediterranean and prized for its fragrant purple blooms, this genus of some 47 flowering plant species belongs to the sage family — name it?
Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.

This American single-engine supersonic interceptor, designed by Kelly Johnson after interviewing Korean War fighter pilots, became part of the 'Century Series' and was widely used as a Cold War fighter-bomber. What is it?
Lockheed F-104 Starfighter is an American single-engine, supersonic interceptor. It was also produced under license by other nations and saw widespread service outside the United States.
A large canine of South America resembling a red fox in markings but being neither fox nor wolf. It's the only species in its genus and the largest canine in South America. What is it?
Maned wolf (Chrysocyon brachyurus) is a large canine of South America.
Aristotle called this the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes the most fundamental structure of reality, from existence itself to the categories of being — what is it?
Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that examines the basic nature or most fundamental structure of reality.
Found naturally in the dark resin of opium and given everywhere from pills to spinal injections, this opiate alters how the brain feels pain — what is it?
Morphine is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
This multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves — their function and their disorders — blending physiology, anatomy, and more — name the field?
Neuroscience is the scientific study of the nervous system (the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system), its functions, and its disorders.
Beginning in the embryo and maturing a primary oocyte into a fertilization-ready egg cell, what is this reproductive process called?
Oogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Named for the extra copy of chromosome 13 found in affected cells, this condition — related to Down and Edwards syndromes — disrupts normal organ development — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome is a syndrome caused by a chromosomal abnormality, in which some or all of the cells of the body contain extra genetic material from chromosome 13.
Prized as an ornamental indoor plant and still poorly understood taxonomically, this arum-family genus ranks second in size only to Anthurium — which genus?
Philodendron is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This category of polymer includes both natural proteins like wool and silk, and synthetic materials like nylon and aramid fibers — what is it?
Polyamide is a polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds.
This noncontagious autoimmune condition leaves dry, scaly patches of skin and can flare at the exact spot of an injury — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon; what is it?
Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.
This rapidly worsening brain condition can follow a bout of chickenpox or influenza and is strongly associated with aspirin use in children — what syndrome is it?
Reye syndrome is a rapidly worsening brain disease. Signs and symptoms of Reye syndrome may include vomiting, personality changes, confusion, seizures, and loss of consciousness.
Named for the Latin word for willow tree, from which it was first derived, this plant hormone is both a precursor to aspirin and a common ingredient in anti-acne skincare — which compound?
Salicylic acid is an organic compound with the formula C7H6O3.

Essentially plasma with the clotting factors and cells removed, this pale yellow fluid still carries antibodies, hormones, and electrolytes and is central to typing tests done before a transfusion — what is it?
Serum (blood) is the fluid and solvent component of blood which does not play a role in clotting.

This genus of about 60 evergreen flowering plant species, native to the tropical Americas and Southeast Asia, is commonly grown as a houseplant valued for its large leaves and elegant white blooms — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum is a genus of about 60 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas and southeastern Asia.
A single-seat, twin-engine, supermaneuverable 4.5-generation fighter derived from the Su-27, it was relabeled from "Su-27M" after the Soviet collapse to court export buyers — which Russian jet?
Sukhoi Su-35 (NATO reporting name: Flanker-E/M, occasionally nicknamed "Super Flanker") is the designation for two improved derivatives of the Su-27 air superiority fighter.
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces the body's hemoglobin production, sometimes causing anemia, an enlarged spleen, and stunted growth in children — what condition is it?
Thalassemia are a group of inherited blood disorders that manifest as the production of reduced hemoglobin.
Not a single branch of the family of life but a strategy evolved over and over — a tall trunk and branches reaching for sunlight — describes which kind of perennial plant?
Tree is a perennial plant with an elongated stem, or trunk, usually supporting branches and leaves.
Regarded as the 'Father of the Indian space program,' this physicist and astronomer also helped develop nuclear power in India, earning the Padma Vibhushan posthumously — who is he?
Vikram Sarabhai (12 August 1919 - 30 December 1971) was an Indian physicist and astronomer who initiated space research and helped to develop nuclear power in India.

Extracted from birch wood and named for the Greek word for 'wood', this white crystalline sugar alcohol is more soluble in water than any other common sugar alcohol except sorbitol. Name the compound?
Xylitol is an organic compound with the formula HOCH(CH(OH)CH2OH)2.
Caused by a mutation in the FGFR3 gene, this genetic disorder is the most common cause of short stature, marked by shortened limbs, a normal-length torso and a prominent forehead — what is it called?
Achondroplasia: Genetic condition, the most common form of dwarfism.
With wingspans reaching up to eleven and a half feet, which large seabird family ranges across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific but is absent from the North Atlantic?
Albatross: Family of large seabirds. The albatrosses are usually regarded as falling into four genera, but disagreement exists over the number of species.
Also known as shadbush, serviceberry, or juneberry, this rose-family shrub's berries inspired the name of a Canadian city — which genus?

Named from Greek words meaning "unlike other shrimp," this extinct arthropod from the Burgess Shale had swimming flaps, big compound eyes and grasping frontal appendages, reaching over a foot long — which prehistoric predator?
Anomalocaris: Extinct genus of cambrian radiodont.

Known only from fragmentary remains including vertebrae and a giant femur first found by a farmer in 1987, this titanosaur may be the largest land animal ever discovered, stretching up to 35 meters — which genus?
Argentinosaurus: Late Cretaceous giant sauropod dinosaur genus.
The famous AL 288-1 skeleton nicknamed 'Lucy,' unearthed in Ethiopia's Afar region, belongs to which extinct East African hominin species that lived roughly 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago?
Australopithecus afarensis: Extinct hominid from the Pliocene of East Africa.
This inflammatory condition causes recurring, painful mouth sores along with eye inflammation and arthritis, and is diagnosed after at least three sore outbreaks in a year — which condition?
Behçet's disease: Inflammatory disorder. Behçet's disease or Behçet's syndrome (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
This small Old World flycatcher breeds in rocky habitats from the British Isles to Morocco and central China, staying put in milder areas but migrating from colder ones — what bird is it?
Black redstart: Species of bird. The black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family.
Formed from the C5-T1 spinal nerve roots, this network of nerves runs through the neck and over the first rib to supply the shoulder, arm, and hand — what is it?
Brachial plexus: Network of nerves. This plexus extends from the spinal cord, through the cervicoaxillary canal in the neck, over the first rib, and into the armpit.
Developed in 1964 at Britain's Royal Radar Establishment and influenced by JOVIAL, this programming language was chosen by the UK Ministry of Defence in 1971 for military applications — what is it?
CORAL: Early programming language. The R was originally for "radar", not "real-time".
Derived from Greek words for 'heart' and 'study,' this branch of internal medicine covers coronary artery disease, heart failure, and electrophysiology — which medical field?
Cardiology: Branch of medicine dealing with the heart.
Triggered by anything from a stroke to a bout of altitude sickness, this dangerous buildup of fluid inside the skull raises pressure on brain tissue and can cause seizures or worse — what is it?
Cerebral edema: Excess accumulation of fluid in the brain.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks, rays, skates, and ghost-like chimaeras — has skeletons made entirely of cartilage rather than bone — what is it called?
Chondrichthyes: Class of jawed cartilaginous fish. Chondrichthyes are aquatic vertebrates with paired fins, paired nares, placoid scales, and conus arteriosus in the heart.
Recognizable by a prominent crest and curved bill, this Australasian parrot family includes 21 species, the smallest of which is the cockatiel — which family of birds?
Cockatoo: Any bird in the family Cacatuidae.
What is this — “Animal sexual reproductive act in which a male introduces sperm into the female's body”?

Copulation (zoology): Animal sexual reproductive act in which a male introduces sperm into the female's body. In zoology, copulation is animal sexual behavior in which a male introduces sperm into the female's body, especially directly into the female's reproductive tract.
This medical sign turns the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes a bluish-purple hue when blood isn't carrying enough oxygen, and comes in central and peripheral forms — what is it called?
Cyanosis: Decreased oxygen in the blood. Cyanosis is apparent usually in the body tissues covered with thin skin, including the mucous membranes, lips, nail beds, and ear lobes.
Often called eczema, this term covers skin inflammation marked by itchiness, redness and rash — sometimes with tiny blisters, sometimes thickening over time. What is it?
Dermatitis: Inflammatory disease of the skin.

Developed in the early 1950s to replace the propeller-driven Skyraider, this US Navy carrier jet had a maximum takeoff weight of just 24,500 pounds — about half the Navy's specification — which aircraft?
Douglas A-4 Skyhawk: Carrier-based attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Also known as the bodhi tree, this species is revered in four South Asian religions as the tree beneath which Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment — which species?
Ficus religiosa: Species of fig. Ficus religiosa or sacred fig is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.

One of the first management consultants, this American mechanical engineer wrote a 1909 book — later voted the most influential management book of the 20th century — and helped found industrial engineering. Who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor: American mechanical engineer (1856–1915)
Combining Greek words for 'earth,' 'form,' and 'study,' what field examines how landscapes and seafloor features form and evolve over time?
This Intel co-founder proposed the famous observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years — who is he?
This inherited disorder leaves blood unable to clot properly, causing prolonged bleeding after injury and, in its two main forms, low levels of clotting factor VIII or IX — which condition?
Haemophilia: Genetic disease involving blood clotting.
Spread mainly through blood-to-blood contact, this viral infection becomes chronic in about 70 percent of those first infected and can lead to liver failure over decades — which disease?
Hepatitis C: Human viral infection. Hepatitis C is an infectious disease caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV) that primarily affects the liver; it is a type of viral hepatitis.

This field, drawing on sociology, anthropology, economics, and environmental science, studies how communities interact with their habitats — from urban sprawl to cultural and economic patterns across space — which discipline?
Human geography: Study of cultures, communities, people, lifestyle, and activities of people of the world.

Named from the Greek word for "fish" because of its dry, scaly skin, this family of genetic skin disorders ranges from a mild type mistaken for ordinary dry skin to a rare, life-threatening form — which condition?
Ichthyosis: Family of disorders causing dry, thickened, scaly skin.

Native to the Americas but now grown worldwide, one species of this flowering plant genus has become such a popular ornamental that it's classified as an invasive weed on four continents — which genus?
Jacaranda: Genus of trees. The generic name is also used as the common name.

The id Software programmer behind Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, and Quake later left to become CTO of Oculus VR — before walking away again to chase artificial general intelligence. Which 3D-graphics wizard is he?
John Carmack: American computer programmer and video game developer (born 1970)
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
At Bologna in the 1700s she became the first woman to hold a science doctorate and the first salaried female university teacher — depicted as the goddess Minerva herself; who was she?
Laura Bassi: Italian physicist and academic (1711–1778)
This soft, movable pair of appendages on the jaw helps with eating and speech, and is often used in kissing — what are they?
Lip: Visible body parts at the mouth.
Named from the Latin for "wolf," this autoimmune disease often announces itself with a red facial rash and alternates between flares and remission — what is it?
Lupus: Autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
Boiled down from its sap to make a beloved breakfast syrup, this genus of roughly 132 tree and shrub species counts the sycamore as its type species — which genus of trees?
Made up of the dura, arachnoid, and pia mater, these three protective membranes shield the brain and spinal cord while containing cerebrospinal fluid — what are they called?
Meninges: Three membranes protecting the brain. In anatomy, the meninges (sing. meninx; from Ancient Greek μῆνινξ (mêninx) 'membrane') are protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord.
This Russian polymath discovered the atmosphere of Venus and formulated the law of conservation of mass, while also helping shape the modern Russian literary language as a poet — who is he?
With roughly 200 species across 16 genera, this family of elongated fish is almost exclusively marine, with a name traced back through Portuguese and Latin to a Greek word — which family?
Moray eel: Family of fishes. Moray eels, or Muraenidae, are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
Sold under the brand name Revia, this medication blocks opioid receptors to reduce cravings in alcohol and opioid use disorders and is combined with bupropion to treat obesity — what is it?
Naltrexone: Medication. It has also been found to be effective for the treatment of other addictions and may be used for them off-label.
Discovered in 1846 by Ascanio Sobrero, this oily explosive liquid became the key ingredient in dynamite — what is it?

Sold under the brand name Zofran, this serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist prevents chemotherapy- and surgery-related nausea without the dopamine-blocking side effects that cause muscle restlessness — what is this drug?
Ondansetron: Medication to prevent nausea and vomiting.
Known for its fragrant leaves used to flavor dishes across Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and Hainanese cuisine, this member of the screwpine genus is prized in many Asian kitchens — which plant?
Pandanus amaryllifolius: Species of tropical plant.
This bony ring connects the spine to the lower limbs at the hip joints, formed by the sacrum, coccyx, and a pair of hip bones — what body region?
Pelvis: Lower torso of the human body.
This colorless, highly toxic pnictogen hydride is pure when odorless, but technical samples reek of rotting fish — and impurities can make it burst into flame in air — what is it?
Named after a French mathematician and physicist, this materials-science measure captures how much a material bulges sideways when compressed lengthwise — what is it?
Poisson's ratio: Measure of material deformation perpendicular to loading.
Found just below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male-only gland acts like a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation — which organ?
Prostate: Gland of the male reproductive system.
Sold as Seroquel and prescribed for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, this atypical antipsychotic is also widely (and questionably) used as a sleep aid for its tranquillizing effect — which drug?
Quetiapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Quetiapine is believed to work by blocking a number of receptors, including those for serotonin and dopamine.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
